evidence_packet.evidence_text: An alleged "close associate" of the Manchester synagogue knife attacker has denied failing to disclose information in relation to the terror attack Worshippers Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby were killed when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, drove into the gates of the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue in October last year, and then began attacking with a knife, wearing a fake suicide belt Hekmat Ali Hakim, 49, of Salford, Greater Manchester, appeared via video link from prison at the Old Bailey on Friday and pleaded not guilty to failing to disclose information Prosecutor Jonathan Polnay KC said the Iraqi national was a "close associate of Jihad Al-Shamie, who carried out a terrorist attack at a synagogue in Manchester" He said Hakim allegedly "failed to disclose that information" The charges state that between 13 August and 3 October last year, Hakim had information which he knew or believed might be of material assistance in preventing the commission by Al-Shamie of an act of terrorism in the UK

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester’s Mayor Bev Craig has sent a message as the region remembers Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby, the survivors and everyone affected by the appalling antisemitic terror attack at Heaton Park Synagogue “Today, Greater Manchester remembers Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby, the survivors and everyone affected by the appalling antisemitic terror attack at Heaton Park Synagogue one year ago.” This was an act of terror against Jewish people on the holiest day of the year, targeted simply for being Jewish. A dark day for our city-region and one we should never have to face again Greater Manchester is a place with a deep history of unity, and an attack on one of our communities is an attack on us all My thoughts remain with the families and loved ones of Melvin, Adrian, those who were injured, and the wider congregation of Heaton Park Synagogue We stand with you in remembrance and solidarity, knowing that words are not enough, and we are committed to acting to stamp out the pernicious rise of antisemitism

evidence_packet.evidence_text: An alleged "close associate" of the Manchester synagogue knife attacker has denied failing to disclose information in relation to the terror attack Worshippers Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby were killed when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, drove into the gates of the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue in October last year, and then began attacking with a knife, wearing a fake suicide belt Hekmat Ali Hakim, 49, of Salford, Greater Manchester, appeared via video link from prison at the Old Bailey on Friday and pleaded not guilty to failing to disclose information Prosecutor Jonathan Polnay KC said the Iraqi national was a "close associate of Jihad Al-Shamie, who carried out a terrorist attack at a synagogue in Manchester" He said Hakim allegedly "failed to disclose that information" The charges state that between 13 August and 3 October last year, Hakim had information which he knew or believed might be of material assistance in preventing the commission by Al-Shamie of an act of terrorism in the UK

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester’s Mayor Bev Craig has sent a message as the region remembers Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby, the survivors and everyone affected by the appalling antisemitic terror attack at Heaton Park Synagogue “Today, Greater Manchester remembers Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby, the survivors and everyone affected by the appalling antisemitic terror attack at Heaton Park Synagogue one year ago.” This was an act of terror against Jewish people on the holiest day of the year, targeted simply for being Jewish. A dark day for our city-region and one we should never have to face again Greater Manchester is a place with a deep history of unity, and an attack on one of our communities is an attack on us all My thoughts remain with the families and loved ones of Melvin, Adrian, those who were injured, and the wider congregation of Heaton Park Synagogue We stand with you in remembrance and solidarity, knowing that words are not enough, and we are committed to acting to stamp out the pernicious rise of antisemitism

evidence_packet.evidence_text: An alleged "close associate" of the Manchester synagogue knife attacker has denied failing to disclose information in relation to the terror attack Worshippers Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby were killed when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, drove into the gates of the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue in October last year, and then began attacking with a knife, wearing a fake suicide belt Hekmat Ali Hakim, 49, of Salford, Greater Manchester, appeared via video link from prison at the Old Bailey on Friday and pleaded not guilty to failing to disclose information Prosecutor Jonathan Polnay KC said the Iraqi national was a "close associate of Jihad Al-Shamie, who carried out a terrorist attack at a synagogue in Manchester" He said Hakim allegedly "failed to disclose that information" The charges state that between 13 August and 3 October last year, Hakim had information which he knew or believed might be of material assistance in preventing the commission by Al-Shamie of an act of terrorism in the UK

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester’s Mayor Bev Craig has sent a message as the region remembers Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby, the survivors and everyone affected by the appalling antisemitic terror attack at Heaton Park Synagogue “Today, Greater Manchester remembers Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby, the survivors and everyone affected by the appalling antisemitic terror attack at Heaton Park Synagogue one year ago.” This was an act of terror against Jewish people on the holiest day of the year, targeted simply for being Jewish. A dark day for our city-region and one we should never have to face again Greater Manchester is a place with a deep history of unity, and an attack on one of our communities is an attack on us all My thoughts remain with the families and loved ones of Melvin, Adrian, those who were injured, and the wider congregation of Heaton Park Synagogue We stand with you in remembrance and solidarity, knowing that words are not enough, and we are committed to acting to stamp out the pernicious rise of antisemitism

evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Last confirmed: 10 September 2026 Event date: 2026-10-04 Venue: Bolton Car Boot Sale Price: £1 Status: https://schema.org/EventScheduled
